issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require Farm to use a List<Animal> (implemented as an ArrayList) for the animals aggregation, but the provided solution implements the animals attribute as a Set<Animal> (HashSet). This is a structural type mismatch: it changes the collection semantic (ordering and duplication) and contradicts the explicit instruction to use ArrayList, which can confuse students and lead to different behaviour (e.g., song ordering, duplicates).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and any tests) with the problem specification by using List<Animal> for the animals attribute and instantiate it as an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. Update the field type, getter/setter signatures, and any usages (iteration, add/remove) accordingly. Alternatively, if a Set is intended, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require a Set and explain the different semantics.
